The letter is written on Holt paper.

The letter is addressed to "Judge Amos Ferris", and the county court's records show Ferris was first appointed a judge in 1803. Someone writing in 1788 would not have called him a judge, so the letter itself points to a date of 1803 or later, which backs the curator independently of the watermark.

Keeping the walls and the loading machinery only saves the silo's historical value if the inside isn't doing any essential work in showing how people lived and worked there. So the argument assumes the interior parts that get gutted aren't essential to its importance. They might add some detail, but the silo's importance doesn't hinge on them.
